correctness.rationale: The relative coordinate has drift −(λ+2k)R, diffusion amplitude √(4D), and a superposed rate-2ω compound Poisson driver with centered Gaussian marks of fixed scale σ. Thinning gives the stated rate q_L. The pathwise integration-by-parts formula gives a simultaneous continuous-in-parameter version of the Brownian convolution. Its supremum on an integer horizon tends to zero by the Brownian modulus of continuity, on one event for all integer horizons. Up to and including the finite first mark above L there are finitely many separated jump times, no mark has magnitude exactly L, and all their distances in magnitude from L have positive minimum. Interjump remnants decay; pre-jump remnants converge to zero at all those times. This yields literal equality of exit times for all sufficiently large real k on the same noise path. At any first jump of magnitude >2L, either exit already occurred or the pre-jump modulus is ≤L, which suffices to force exit: this gives an exponential dominator for every positive real power. For the variance-rate-matched Brownian model, the generator is Θ∂²−ax∂, with Θ=2D+ωσ². Integrating the symmetric backward solution and applying Gaussian saturation and endpoint Laplace asymptotics gives the stated prefactor and rate.
residual_risks: Fixed jump size refers to fixed nonzero scale of the Gaussian mark law, not deterministic mark magnitude. Finite D=0 simulation cannot verify the D>0 or all-real-k pathwise result; those follow from the proof.

The supported 'noncommutation' is the fixed-mark stiffness asymptotic versus Gaussian replacement before that asymptotic. The record does not define a Gaussianization parameter or establish unequal raw iterated limits in a joint two-parameter family.

Rescaling time by a fixes the restoring rate but divides the shot rate by a and the Brownian amplitude by √a, leaving each mark distribution unchanged. Goel–Marathe adiabatically eliminate the relative mode before computing the center-of-mass first passage.

The supported distinct claim is eventual equality with a specified common-noise jump at fixed physical mark law and increasing stiffness, with convergence of all positive moments and the explicit variance-matched contrast for relative bond rupture. Goel–Marathe §III.2, motivating stiffness and Gaussian approximation comparison
value.rationale: For a natural relative-extension threshold, the theorem identifies precisely a failure of second-moment matching for an exit observable: the shot-driven mean has a finite limit while the matched diffusion mean grows exponentially with known prefactor. The stronger common-noise equality and all-moments conclusion distinguish this from a simulation observation or informal single-jump heuristic.
residual_risks: The model requires an instantaneous kick with nonzero superthreshold probability and assumes a harmonic relative mode. It does not quantify finite-duration kicks, the motivating nonlinear dimer's well-to-well passage, or a general error bound for a diffusion approximation.
